site.name: Hagerman Trestle
site.componentDetail: Former 1,084-foot curved Colorado Midland timber trestle on the eastern approach to Hagerman Tunnel
overview: Hagerman Trestle was a major timber railroad structure on the Colorado Midland route west of Leadville, built along the eastern approach to the Hagerman Tunnel near the Continental Divide.
The trestle should be interpreted as part of the broader Hagerman Pass railroad landscape, together with the tunnel, grade, cuts, fills, snow-control works, and construction-camp remains.

timeline.text: The Colorado Midland completed the Hagerman Tunnel route across the Continental Divide and built the large curved trestle on its eastern approach.
The lower Busk-Ivanhoe route replaced the severe Hagerman Tunnel crossing for regular operations.
The older Hagerman route saw limited later use before being abandoned as the railroad shifted to the lower crossing.
The former railroad grade and trestle site remain part of the historic Hagerman Pass transportation landscape.

moreHistory: USGS historical-trail documentation describes Hagerman Trestle as 1,084 feet long, about 84 feet high, and curved roughly 200 degrees along the eastern approach to Hagerman Pass and Hagerman Tunnel.
Because the structure was long and curved, Remnant uses an approach-level identification anchor rather than presenting a fabricated single-point center for the entire former trestle.
